topics.title: California is about to make it illegal for an algorithm to fire you alone.
topics.why: SB 947 (the 'No Robo Bosses Act') and AB 1883 (bans emotion-inference and neural-data surveillance at work) sit on Newsom's desk with a Sep 30 deadline; Connecticut's version is already law. First issue on what the rules actually give a worker, not on job counts.

topics.title: Half your coworkers are pasting company data into AI. Security teams can now see every paste.
topics.why: Verizon's 2026 DBIR: regular AI use on corporate devices jumped from 15% to 45% in a year, two-thirds of it through accounts the company doesn't control, and the median org logs ~50 attempted leaks to AI tools a day. A practical 'how not to become an incident' issue.

topics.title: The AI agent just got its own login. Here's what changes when it has your permissions.
topics.why: OpenAI's Data agent in ChatGPT Work (Sep 9), Meta's Muse for Mac, Salesforce agents inside Slack: September's shift is from chat tools to agents acting across your systems. What to grant, what to refuse, and what your job looks like as the reviewer.

topics.title: Anthropic just paid $1.5 billion for training data. About $3,000 a book. Here's what your work is worth.
topics.why: The Bartz settlement is one of the largest copyright payouts in U.S. history, with 25+ similar cases pending against OpenAI, Meta and GitHub. An issue on what it means for anyone whose writing, code or designs are already training data.

topics.title: 13 new models shipped this month. Here's the 4 that actually change how you work.
topics.why: Claude Fable 5.1, Gemini 3.8 Flash and a dozen others landed in September, and daily AI use among U.S. adults more than doubled between March and August. A hands-on tools issue instead of a labor-market one: what to switch, what to ignore, what it costs.
